title: Stine-Morrow (2007): Multiple Choice
instructions: Choose the answer that best preserves the article's conceptual distinctions, study designs, and limits of the evidence.

items.prompt: Which pair captures the two forces commonly used to explain cognitive aging?
options: Declining crystallized abilities and steadily increasing fluid abilities
Declining mental mechanics and accumulated cultural competence
Complete loss of processing speed and perfect preservation of knowledge
Simultaneous increases in social expectations and intellectual opportunities
items.answer: Declining mental mechanics and accumulated cultural competence
items.explanation: The article contrasts senescence-related declines in mental mechanics with experience that builds cultural, practical, and knowledge-based competence.

options: Effective allocation of attention to the processes supporting a current task
Selecting only intellectually demanding occupations for long-term comparison
Training every cognitive ability simultaneously through one standardized exercise
Statistically removing all educational, occupational, and genetic influences
items.answer: Effective allocation of attention to the processes supporting a current task
items.explanation: It concerns implementing task-specific operations, such as organization and elaboration, and differs from choosing intellectually stimulating environments.

options: Automatically shifting gaze according to the length of each word
Pausing briefly to integrate the meaning of the current sentence
Habitually choosing settings with novel, ill-defined intellectual challenges
Lowering the accuracy criterion whenever a reading task becomes difficult
items.answer: Habitually choosing settings with novel, ill-defined intellectual challenges
items.explanation: The article describes self-directed participation in real-life contexts that require selecting, prioritizing, and structuring unfamiliar problems.

items.prompt: Which three representation levels appear in the SRLP model?
options: Sensation, movement, emotion, and motivation
Memory, processing speed, and reasoning ability
Attention, executive control, mindfulness, and self-efficacy
Surface form, textbase, and situation model
items.answer: Surface form, textbase, and situation model
items.explanation: Understanding and memory involve the words, their semantic content, and a representation of the situation described by the text.

items.prompt: How does the negative feedback loop in SRLP regulate effort?
options: It removes the comprehension criterion and always shortens reading time
It compares comprehension with a criterion and recruits resources to close a shortfall
It compares ability with an age-group average and abandons demanding tasks
It stops constructing all other representations once surface form is complete
items.answer: It compares comprehension with a criterion and recruits resources to close a shortfall
items.explanation: Cognitive and socioemotional goals shape reference values. Additional resources are demanded until perceived comprehension meets the criterion.

items.prompt: What did the accuracy-versus-efficiency reading study actually find?
options: Neither age group changed reading time with either goals or informational density
Only older readers increased time as density rose, equally under both instructions
Younger readers were more responsive to the accuracy goal, especially at higher density
Older readers consistently spent longer than younger readers on every sentence
items.answer: Younger readers were more responsive to the accuracy goal, especially at higher density
items.explanation: Figure 2 shows younger adults allocating extra reading time under accuracy instructions, particularly for denser material. Older adults were less responsive to the stricter acquisition criterion.

items.prompt: How did memory self-efficacy relate to age differences in goal responsiveness?
options: It explained part of the difference alongside working-memory capacity
It was identical to actual memory capacity and added no separate belief component
It independently eliminated every age difference in reading and recall performance
It was an unrelated personality characteristic with no connection to accuracy goals
items.answer: It explained part of the difference alongside working-memory capacity
items.explanation: The findings suggest that beliefs about influencing memory outcomes, as well as existing capacity, may affect willingness to recruit effort.

items.prompt: Why do correlations between an engaged lifestyle and cognition not settle causation?
options: Intellectual activity cannot be measured reliably in any real-life setting
No valid cognitive measures have been developed for use with older adults
All intellectually active people have identical educational and occupational histories
Selection and common-cause explanations remain plausible
items.answer: Selection and common-cause explanations remain plausible
items.explanation: People with greater initial vitality may select and maintain activities, or activity and cognition may both reflect an underlying process.

items.prompt: How does the article interpret education-related tolerance of Alzheimer's pathology?
options: Education directly removes pathology and completely prevents disease onset
The pattern is consistent with cognitive reserve and is harder to explain by simple selection
The review excludes all evidence on education and tolerance of brain pathology
The evidence shows less educated people tolerating equivalent pathology for longer
items.answer: The pattern is consistent with cognitive reserve and is harder to explain by simple selection
items.explanation: Cognitive reserve proposes alternative neural repertoires developed through rich experience. The article does not newly establish a direct causal effect of education or eliminate every selection explanation.

items.prompt: Which description of the ACTIVE trial is accurate?
options: Everyone received lifelong training in memory, speed, and reasoning without random assignment
Researchers retrospectively compared naturally active and inactive older adults
Older adults were randomized to memory, speed, or reasoning training or no-contact control
Only self-reports from Senior Odyssey participants were collected
items.answer: Older adults were randomized to memory, speed, or reasoning training or no-contact control
items.explanation: Training comprised ten sessions in a targeted ability, and retention of training effects was demonstrated for up to five years.

items.prompt: Which finding illustrates the specificity of ACTIVE training effects?
options: Speed training improved speeded tasks without transfer to memory or reasoning
Every training condition transferred equally to all cognitive and daily-life outcomes
All training effects vanished immediately when the sessions ended
Only the no-contact controls improved in speed, memory, and reasoning
items.answer: Speed training improved speeded tasks without transfer to memory or reasoning
items.explanation: Training effects persisted but were specific. Transfer to everyday analogues had not been demonstrated, although reasoning trainees reported greater ease with instrumental daily activities.

items.prompt: What puzzle does the author identify across lifestyle, training, and expertise research?
options: Both observational and experimental studies found no experience-related cognitive differences
Experimental training transferred broadly, while lifestyle associations involved only one skill
Everyday activity could not be defined or measured in a form suitable for research
Lifestyle associations were broad, but training effects were ability-specific
items.answer: Lifestyle associations were broad, but training effects were ability-specific
items.explanation: An engaged lifestyle may exercise a wider range of abilities. The author presents that explanation as plausible while emphasizing how little its mechanisms had been explored.

options: Repeated individual memorization of questions with one predetermined answer
Ill-defined problems, spontaneous challenges, creativity, choice, and teamwork
Elimination of participant choice and prohibition of every form of competition
Strict separation from existing educational programs and younger age groups
items.answer: Ill-defined problems, spontaneous challenges, creativity, choice, and teamwork
items.explanation: The program also used friendly competition and links to Odyssey of the Mind to build on existing structures and encourage age integration.

items.prompt: Which summary preserves the scope of the preliminary Senior Odyssey findings?
options: Large improvements in all abilities and daily functions were definitively established, ending the need for research
Neither processing speed nor divergent thinking changed relative to controls
Speed improved, divergent thinking improved marginally, and engagement dispositions increased
Memory alone improved while mindfulness and need for cognition declined
items.answer: Speed improved, divergent thinking improved marginally, and engagement dispositions increased
items.explanation: Relative to wait-list controls, participants improved in speed, marginally in divergent thinking, and in mindfulness and need for cognition. Broad cognitive improvement remained unestablished.

items.prompt: Which statement best captures the Dumbledore hypothesis in the conclusion?
options: Senescence does not exist, and present choices alone determine every cognitive difference
Repeating one exercise necessarily improves all memory, speed, and reasoning abilities
Childhood ability completely fixes cognitive vitality for the rest of life
Vitality may depend on how people engage tasks and which abilities those activities develop
items.answer: Vitality may depend on how people engage tasks and which abilities those activities develop
items.explanation: The author calls for tests of the interaction between attentional and activity engagement, including possible roles of novelty, self-efficacy, control, and mindfulness.
